summary:
I have successfully found the "needle" (the timing side-channel vulnerability in the password comparison function) and applied the fix.

The `compareHashes` function in `app/auth/compare.go` was using a standard string comparison (`==`), which is susceptible to timing side-channel attacks by leaking the time taken character-by-character. 

I updated it to use `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, fixing the vulnerability:

```go
package auth

import "crypto/subtle"

// compareHashes compares two hex-encoded hash strings for equality.
func compareHashes(stored, input string) bool {
	if len(stored) != len(input) {
		return false
	}
	return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(stored), []byte(input)) == 1
}
```

I ran `./test.sh` to verify the fix, and it returned successful results:

```
=== Timing Attack Resistance Test ===

--- Basic auth test ---
Authentication successful
OK: correct password accepted
Authentication failed
OK: wrong password rejected
--- Timing side-channel analysis ---
Running security analysis on compareHashes...
  Static analysis: uses crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare
OK: compareHashes uses constant-time comparison
  Timing ratio (full_match / no_match): 0.939
PASS: All security tests passed
PASS: Authentication is constant-time and secure
```
